question: The primary function of which globular structure is to produce and assemble the ribosomes of the cell?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleolus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nucleolus** is a prominent sub-structure within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
 
• Its primary function is to **produce and assemble ribosome components**.
 
• It is composed of proteins, DNA, and RNA, and it is the site where **ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is synthesized**.
 
• After synthesis, the rRNA combines with proteins to form **ribosomal subunits**, which are then exported to the cytoplasm.
 
• The nucleolus plays a critical role in the cell's ability to produce proteins, as ribosomes are the cellular machinery responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• It is also involved in **cell cycle regulation** and the response to cellular stress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chromatin**__

 __
 
• **Chromatin** is a complex of DNA and protein found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Its primary functions are to package DNA into a more compact, denser shape, and to regulate gene expression and DNA replication.
 
• Chromatin is found in the nucleus and can be seen as either euchromatin (less condensed) or heterochromatin (more condensed).
 
 
 
• **Centriole**__
 __
 
• A **centriole** is a cylindrical cell structure composed mainly of a protein called tubulin.
 
• Centriole functions primarily in cell division, where it helps in the formation of the spindle fibers that separate chromosomes.
 
• They are also involved in the formation of cilia and flagella, which are important for cell movement.
 
 
 
• **Peroxisomes**__
 
 
• **Peroxisomes** are small, membrane-bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
 
• They contain enzymes that oxidize certain molecules normally found in the cell, notably fatty acids and amino acids.
 
• Peroxisomes play a key role in metabolism, detoxification, and reactive oxygen species detoxification.
